questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause excessive oil use.
Require your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner than normal.
Make you drowsy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine and cools hot gases. A leak can let dangerous fumes into your vehicle. These fumes can make you drowsy while driving and can be deadly.

questions.question: When you stop at an intersection, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go through when it is safe, this matches:

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars following too closely.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to make sure no cars are coming from that direction.

questions.question: Unless a sign says otherwise, the speed limit on an open county highway is:

options.text: 70 mph.
65 mph.
60 mph.
55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The normal speed limit on open county highways is 55 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change to check your blind spots.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What colors are used on signs showing the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that give information about destinations are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side. Wait until you can drive completely through without blocking the intersection.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. You must drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather. Adjust your speed if conditions make the posted limit unsafe.

questions.question: While waiting in an intersection to turn left, you should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, this prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text on it to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with just one rider.
You must move your entire vehicle into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
Motorcycle brake lights turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move your entire vehicle into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs show that a railroad crossing is ahead. Watch for trains when you see this sign.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look in all directions, then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, you should be ready to yield to vehicles coming from the right. Stay prepared by easing off the gas, covering the brake, and checking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road with two-way traffic, you must use the lane meant for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If a car with high beams comes toward you, look toward the ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right side
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has high beams and does not dim them, glance to the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your side of the road until the car passes.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following, except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A no passing zone.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot of a large vehicle.
An area for motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Avoid staying in these blind spots.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and vehicles with a driver and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they can and cannot do in an area. They show speed limits, no passing rules, no turning rules, and other driving laws.

questions.question: If a car with Anti-Lock Brakes starts to slip on a wet road, what should the driver do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If the car loses grip, press hard on the brake pedal and keep pressing it while steering away from danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) pumps the brakes automatically and very fast. If you pump the brakes or release the brake pedal, the ABS will not work.

questions.question: If a green turn arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn without waiting.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn the way the arrow pointed. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane that has the broken line.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the least traffic.
On the same side where traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the most traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they face the traffic coming toward them.
